statement.p: Find the the general antiderivative F(x) of the function f(x) given below. Note that you can check your answer by differentiation.

static.solution: \int\,9 x^{3} \cos(x^{4})\,dx. We use substitution with w = x^{4} to find this. We have dw = 4\,x^{3}\,dx, so that \int\,9 x^{3} \cos(x^{4})\,dx = {9\over 4}\int\,\cos(w)\,dw = {9\over 4}\,\sin(w) + C = {9\over 4}\,\sin(x^{4}) + C.
